principles.text: Don't short into downside extension (Russell extended): wait for the bounce into resistance rather than chase; patience for better entries over action.

Sector strength decides the side: software is strong (pullback to the weekly 9, weekly uptrend), semis are under all EMAs in a downtrend, so shorts go in semis, not software. A name in a strong sector is 'not a short'.
Headlines (e.g. AI-policy news) are interesting stories but irrelevant to trading decisions; he trades price action, like Darvas.
Does not use market breadth or put/call ratios; decisions come from names in his screens and watchlists.
Very large positions (gold ~2x silver, silver 35-40%) are acceptable in slow movers (low ATR) with no earnings and little overnight-gap catalyst, especially when the trade works right after entry.
Risk per trade lowered to ~0.3% on average this year.
In a weak market avoid longs entirely; short-base / extension breakouts only work in strong markets (e.g. April). Prefer a longer consolidation or deeper pullback for extended leaders like MRNA.
A short-side hold stays fine while price is under the declining 9 EMA; concern starts only if it takes out the previous-day high and gets above the declining 9.
A non-ideal-timing short is acceptable only with a clean rejection and a tight stop, and kept small (one name, 'nothing crazy'); when the market really weakens there will be many shortable bounces.
In a losing stretch, look for commonalities in losers AND in passed winners: sector strength, entry location (at extensions?), stop placement; some of it is luck on a small sample.
